title: MIT Bengaluru Inaugurates Q-HUB@MAHE and Deploys QuantrolOx's Open-Architecture VIDYAQAR Quantum System - Quantum Computing Report
gist: MIT Bengaluru (MAHE) inaugurated Q-HUB@MAHE on October 13, 2026, with QuantrolOx's open-architecture VIDYAQAR quantum system live, backed by a Finnish/Dutch/Swedish consortium (QuantrolOx, Bluefors, Qblox, ConScience) under India's National Quantum Mission. Phase 1 uses a 25-qubit-capable platform, with a roadmap to 150 and eventually 1,000+ qubits and a goal to train 100 quantum engineers by December 2026.

insights.claim: Manipal Institute of Technology Bengaluru inaugurated the Manipal House of Quantum (Q-HUB@MAHE) on October 13, 2026, with QuantrolOx's VIDYAQAR open-architecture quantum system live as its technical centerpiece under India's National Quantum Mission.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Signals India's state-backed quantum program is creating real hardware demand for European quantum suppliers.

insights.claim: The Q-HUB facility formalizes a multi-vendor consortium via Memorandums of Agreement between QuantrolOx (Finland), Bluefors (Finland), Qblox (Netherlands) and ConScience (Sweden) to build open quantum infrastructure in India.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: European quantum component vendors are bundling into consortia to win emerging-market national programs.
insights.quote: a multi-vendor consortium formalizing Memorandums of Agreement between QuantrolOx (Finland), Bluefors (Finland), Qblox (Netherlands), and ConScience (Sweden) to build open quantum infrastructure in India

themes.theme: Phased qubit scaling roadmap and workforce targets

insights.claim: Q-HUB@MAHE starts with a 25-qubit-capable dilution refrigeration platform as Phase 1 of a national roadmap targeting 150-qubit proof-of-concept platforms and ultimately industrial-grade systems exceeding 1,000 qubits.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Lays out a multi-phase procurement path that could drive repeat orders for cryogenics and control hardware.
insights.quote: targets scaling to 150-qubit proof-of-concept platforms and ultimately industrial-grade systems exceeding 1,000 qubits

insights.claim: The Q-HUB initiative aims to train 100 quantum engineers by December 2026 to address global quantum workforce shortages, after MAHE faculty and students completed hands-on training at QuantrolOx's facilities at QuTech and the House of Quantum in Delft.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Talent scarcity is a binding constraint on quantum scaling; workforce programs are part of vendor go-to-market.
insights.quote: aims to train 100 quantum engineers by December 2026

themes.theme: Open, modular quantum testbed versus vendor lock-in

insights.claim: QuantrolOx's VIDYAQAR platform is designed to solve quantum hardware vendor lock-in by letting researchers test, replace and benchmark individual sub-assemblies such as QPUs, parametric amplifiers, cryogenic cabling and control electronics via custom Python workflows in the Quantum EDGE SDK.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Open modular stacks favor component specialists and software/automation layers over vertically integrated full-stack vendors.
insights.quote: designed to solve vendor lock-in by providing a fully open, modular quantum computing testbed

insights.claim: The VIDYAQAR stack combines a ConScience QiB2 7-qubit superconducting QPU, a Bluefors LD 400 dilution refrigerator, Qblox Cluster modular control electronics and QuantrolOx Quantum EDGE automation software.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Shows which specific vendors hold each layer of an open-architecture superconducting stack.

insights.claim: By pairing automated QPU bring-up and characterization software with interchangeable hardware layers, VIDYAQAR lets researchers prototype indigenous quantum components while running one-click calibration workflows.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Calibration automation lowers the barrier for national programs to develop domestic quantum components.
insights.quote: allows researchers to prototype indigenous quantum components while executing one-click calibration workflows

insights.claim: The VIDYAQAR deployment complements QuantrolOx's 5-year QPU industrialization partnership with UC Berkeley and expands its Quantum EDGE Academy workforce initiative with QURECA.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: QuantrolOx is building a portfolio of academic and training partnerships that broaden its control-automation footprint.
insights.quote: complements QuantrolOx’s 5-year QPU industrialization partnership with UC Berkeley
